newsitem.title: USA: FEATURE-Orgasm still tops under new Cosmo editor.
newsitem.headline: FEATURE-Orgasm still tops under new Cosmo editor.

text.p: A new editor has taken over from the legendary Helen Gurley Brown at Cosmopolitian Magazine, but readers need not fear: the orgasm articles are bigger and better than ever.

If you were fretting that new leadership in an age of safe sex and even (shudder) no sex might mute Cosmo's fabled frankness, you can take comfort from the cover of the very first issue edited by Brown's successor, Bonnie Fuller.

Right under the name Cosmopolitan are the words "HIS & HER ORGASMS" in big, black, bold type. And inside the 318-page perfumed issue are two full articles on a subject dear to Cosmo readers -- how to achieve better orgasms (slow him down, speed her up) and whether a woman should fake it if she fails. (A majority of women say faking is OK; a majority of men say if women want to be actreses they should go to Hollywood.)
Who could ask for anything more?

New editor Fuller, a 40-year-old mother of two who is expecting a third child in March, says she has no intention of making radical changes in a magazine that has forged a unique place in the hearts of career women everywhere with its unabashed devotion to female sexual fulfilment, weight loss, successful careers, meeting Mr. Right, interviews with dishy guys, sexy clothing and recipes.

In the 30 years that she edited Cosmo, Brown, author of the pioneering bestseller "Sex and the Single Girl," built a domestic circulation of 2.5 million with revenues of $156.3 million a year plus millions more in 29 international editions. Brown retired at 74 from editing the domestic edition although she remains editor-in-chief of the international editions.

Her theory was that a woman should have everything she wants as long as it isn't fattening, and her creation was as seismic an event for women's magazines as Hugh Heffner's "Playboy" was for men's magazines. When Brown left Cosmo with the February issue, it was with a grand sendoff that summed up all of the themes that made her and Cosmo famous, including articles on "How to Be Very Good in Bed," "How Far Should You Go to Please Him," "How to Be Kissable All Over" and "What to Do When His Car Excites Him More Than You Do."
(Answers to the latter problem included this advice: "Attach fuzzy dice, like tassels, to your breasts. Tie him to the bed with jumper cables and whisper your battery needs a charge.")
Brown even said in a farewell editorial that sex was one of the three best things in life -- but she could not remember the other two.

It is a hard act to follow but Fuller is confident she will keep Cosmo youthful, thin and sexy. "My job is to make sure people keep on buying the magazine," she said, and she spent hours talking about that subject with Brown.

"She was very gracious. ... Stepping into such hallowed footsteps is very intimidating but I feel our philosophies are very similar. I've always subscribed to the Cosmo girl philosophy, not that you can have it all but that life is a great challenge and not something to be feared."

The Canadian-born Fuller honed her skills as a fashion journalist for the Toronto Star, even doing a piece on what it is like to wear a bikini. She has that article framed on her office wall, along with pictures of her husband and children.

She has some changes planned for the magazines, including a letters column and engaging in active conversations with readers on the Internet. But she says, "My mission is not to let the reader know there is a change."
